data.bottom_line: Glide avalanches are releasing daily, without warning, and without a visible crack preceding the release. This is an especially dangerous and tricky problem to manage because we don't know where the next glide avalanche will occur and there may be no visible clue. Choosing places to ski and ride where there are no obvious cracks in the area is our best idea to manage this problem. SUNDAY OUTLOOK: Calm weather is forecast for the weekend so conditions should remain similar tomorrow with glide avalanches being the main concern. __________________________________ SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENTS: Forecast Operations: Chugach State Park - Weekly danger ratings on Saturday begin today. Turnagain Pass - Daily danger ratings begin today. Summit Lake - Twice per week danger ratings on Saturday and Wednesday begin this week. Seward - To be determined based on access conditions, but we will issue a product on December 1 for the motorized opener described below. On December 2nd and 3rd, the Northern Aspects Film Festival 2026 will be showing at Bear Tooth Theatrepub for its fifth year, celebrating the people, places, and stories that make skiing in Alaska unlike anywhere else. These showings will benefit the Hatcher Pass Avalanche Center and the Valdez Avalanche Center. Hope to see you there! Motorized Winter Access: Turnagain Pass opened to snowmachines on Wednesday, November 25 per the CNF Forest plan and the new over-snow vehicle use map ( OSVU map ). The remaining motorized winter riding areas on the Chugach National Forest will open December 1.
